paragraphs: This Annual Report on Form 10-K and the documents incorporated herein by reference contain forward-looking statements based on expectations, estimates, and projections as of the date of this filing. Actual results and outcomes may differ materially from those expressed in forward-looking statements. See Item 1A of Part I — "Risk Factors." As used herein, "Amazon.com," "we," "our," and similar terms include Amazon.com, Inc. and its subsidiaries, unless the context indicates otherwise.

We seek to be Earth's most customer-centric company. We are guided by four principles: customer obsession rather than competitor focus, passion for invention, commitment to operational excellence, and long-term thinking. In each of our segments, we serve our primary customer sets, consisting of consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, content creators, advertisers, and employees.

We have organized our operations into three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services ("AWS"). These segments reflect the way the Company evaluates its business performance and manages its operations. Information on our net sales is contained in Item 8 of Part II, "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data — Note 10 — Segment Information."

We serve consumers through our online and physical stores and focus on selection, price, and convenience. We design our stores to enable hundreds of millions of unique products to be sold by us and by third parties across dozens of product categories. Customers access our offerings through our websites, mobile apps, Alexa, devices, streaming, and physically visiting our stores. We also manufacture and sell electronic devices, including Kindle, Fire tablet, Fire TV, Echo, Ring, Blink, and eero, and we develop and produce media content. We seek to offer our customers low prices, fast and free delivery, easy-to-use functionality, and timely customer service. In addition, we offer subscription services such as Amazon Prime, a membership program that includes fast, free shipping on tens of millions of items, access to award-winning movies and series, live sports, and other benefits.

We fulfill customer orders in a number of ways, including through: North America and International fulfillment networks that we operate; co-sourced and outsourced arrangements in certain countries; digital delivery; and through our physical stores. We operate customer service centers globally, which are supplemented by co-sourced arrangements. See Item 2 of Part I, "Properties."

We offer programs that enable sellers to grow their businesses, sell their products in our stores, and fulfill orders using our services. We are not the seller of record in these transactions. We earn fixed fees, a percentage of sales, per-unit activity fees, interest, or some combination thereof, for our seller programs.

We serve developers and enterprises of all sizes, including start-ups, government agencies, and academic institutions, through AWS, which offers a broad set of on-demand technology services, including compute, storage, database, analytics, artificial intelligence and machine learning, and other services.
We offer programs that allow authors, independent publishers, musicians, filmmakers, Twitch streamers, skill and app developers, and others to publish and sell content.
We provide advertising services to sellers, vendors, publishers, authors, and others, through programs such as sponsored ads, display, and video advertising.

Our businesses encompass a large variety of product types, service offerings, and delivery channels. The worldwide marketplace in which we compete is evolving rapidly and intensely competitive, and we face a broad array of competitors from many different industry sectors around the world. Our current and potential competitors include: (1) physical, e-commerce, and omnichannel retailers, publishers, vendors, distributors, manufacturers, and producers of the products we offer and sell to consumers and businesses; (2) publishers, producers, and distributors of physical, digital, and interactive media of all types and all distribution channels; (3) web search engines, comparison shopping websites, social networks, web portals, virtual assistants, and other online and app-based means of discovering, using, or acquiring goods and services, either directly or in collaboration with other retailers, including through artificial intelligence; (4) companies that provide e-commerce services, including website development and hosting, omnichannel sales, inventory and supply chain management, advertising, fulfillment, customer service, and payment processing; (5) companies that provide fulfillment and logistics services for themselves or for third parties, whether online or offline; (6) companies that provide information technology services or products, including on-premises or cloud-based infrastructure, tools and services relating to artificial intelligence, and other services; (7) companies that design, manufacture, market, or sell consumer electronics, communications, and other electronic devices and services; (8) companies that sell grocery products online and in physical stores; (9) companies that provide advertising services, whether in digital or other formats; and (10) providers of virtual or in-person healthcare services. We believe that the principal competitive factors in our retail businesses include selection, price, and convenience, including fast and reliable fulfillment. Additional competitive factors for our seller and enterprise services include the quality, speed, and reliability of our services and tools, as well as customers' ability and willingness to change business practices. Some of our current and potential competitors have greater resources, longer histories, more customers, greater brand recognition, and greater control over inputs critical to our various businesses. They may secure better terms from suppliers, adopt more aggressive pricing, pursue restrictive distribution agreements that restrict our access to supply, direct consumers to their own offerings instead of ours, lock-in potential customers with restrictive terms, and devote more resources to technology, infrastructure, fulfillment, and marketing. The internet and other technologies including artificial intelligence facilitate competitive entry and comparison shopping, which enhances the ability of new, smaller, or lesser-known businesses to compete against us. Each of our businesses is also subject to rapid change and the development of new business models and the entry of new and well-funded competitors. Other companies also may enter into business combinations or alliances that strengthen their competitive positions.

We regard our trademarks, service marks, copyrights, patents, domain names, trade dress, trade secrets, proprietary technologies, and similar intellectual property as critical to our success, and we rely on trademark, copyright, and patent law, trade-secret protection, and confidentiality and/or license agreements with our employees, customers, partners, and others to protect our proprietary rights. We have registered, or applied for the registration of, a number of U.S. and international domain names, trademarks, service marks, and copyrights. Additionally, we have filed U.S. and international patent applications covering certain of our proprietary technology.
Our business is affected by seasonality, which historically has resulted in higher sales volume during our fourth quarter, which ends December 31.

Our employees are critical to our mission of being Earth's most customer-centric company. As of December 31, 2025, we employed approximately 1,576,000 full-time and part-time employees. Additionally, we use independent contractors and temporary personnel to supplement our workforce. Competition for qualified personnel is intense, particularly for software engineers, computer scientists, and other technical staff (including for artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies), and constrained labor markets have increased competition for personnel across other parts of our business.

We strive to be Earth's best employer. We rely on numerous and evolving initiatives to implement this objective and invent mechanisms for talent development, including competitive pay and benefits, flexible work arrangements, and skills training and educational programs such as Amazon Career Choice (education funding for eligible employees). Over 300,000 Amazon employees around the world have participated in Career Choice. We also continue to inspect and refine the mechanisms we use to hire, develop, evaluate, and retain our employees. In addition, safety is integral to everything we do at Amazon and we continue to invest in safety improvements such as capital improvements, new safety technology, vehicle safety controls, and engineering ergonomic solutions. Our safety team is dedicated to using the science of safety to solve complex problems and establish new industry best practices. We also provide mentorship and support resources to our employees, and have deployed numerous programs that advance employee engagement, communication, and feedback.

paragraphs: Please carefully consider the following discussion of significant factors, events, and uncertainties that make an investment in our securities risky. The events and consequences discussed in these risk factors could, in circumstances we may or may not be able to accurately predict, recognize, or control, have a material adverse effect on our business, growth, reputation, prospects, financial condition, operating results (including components of our financial results), cash flows, liquidity, and stock price. These risk factors do not identify all risks that we face; our operations could also be affected by factors, events, or uncertainties that are not presently known to us or that we currently do not consider to present significant risks to our operations. In addition to the factors discussed in Item 7 of Part II, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," and in the risk factors below, global economic and geopolitical conditions and additional or unforeseen circumstances, developments, or events may give rise to or amplify many of the risks discussed below. Many of the risks discussed below also impact our customers, including third-party sellers, which could indirectly have a material adverse effect on us. The disclosures in this section reflect our beliefs and opinions as to factors that could materially and adversely affect us in the future. References to past events are provided by way of example only and are not intended to be a complete listing or a representation as to whether or not such factors have occurred in the past.

Our businesses are rapidly evolving and intensely competitive, and we have many competitors across geographies, including cross-border competition, and in different industries, including physical, e-commerce, and omnichannel retail, e-commerce services, web and infrastructure computing services, electronic devices, digital content, advertising, grocery, healthcare, communications, and transportation and logistics services. Some of our current and potential competitors have greater resources, longer histories, more customers, and/or greater brand recognition, particularly with our newly-launched products and services and in our newer geographic regions. They may secure better terms from vendors, adopt more aggressive pricing, and devote more resources to technology, infrastructure, fulfillment, and marketing.

Competition continues to intensify, including with the development of new business models and the entry of new and well-funded competitors, and as our competitors enter into business combinations or alliances and established companies in other market segments expand to become competitive with our business. In addition, new and enhanced technologies, including search, web and infrastructure computing services, practical applications of artificial intelligence and machine learning, digital content, satellites, and electronic devices continue to increase our competition. The internet and other technologies including artificial intelligence facilitate competitive entry and comparison shopping, which enhances the ability of new, smaller, or lesser-known businesses to compete against us. As a result of competition, our product and service offerings may not be successful, we may fail to gain or may lose business, and we may be required to increase our spending or lower prices, any of which could materially reduce our sales and profits.

We may have limited or no experience in our newer market segments, and our customers may not adopt our product or service offerings. These offerings, which can present new and difficult technology challenges, may subject us to claims if customers of these offerings experience, or are otherwise impacted by, service disruptions, delays, setbacks, or failures or

quality issues. In addition, profitability or other intended benefits, if any, in our newer activities (including development and adoption of automation, artificial intelligence, and machine learning technologies for customer and internal use), may not meet our expectations, and we may not be successful enough in these newer activities to recoup our investments in them, which investments are often significant. Failure to realize the benefits of amounts we invest in new technologies, products, or services could result in the value of those investments being written down or written off. In addition, our sustainability initiatives may be unsuccessful for a variety of reasons, including if we are unable to realize the expected benefits of new technologies or if we do not successfully plan or execute new strategies, which could harm our business or damage our reputation.

Our international activities are significant to our revenues and profits, and we plan to further expand internationally. In certain international market segments, we have relatively little operating experience and may not benefit from any first-to-market advantages or otherwise succeed. It is costly to establish, develop, and maintain international operations and stores, and promote our brand internationally. Our international operations may not become profitable on a sustained basis.

paragraphs: This Annual Report on Form 10-K includes forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. All statements other than statements of historical fact, including statements regarding guidance, industry prospects, or future results of operations or financial position, made in this Annual Report on Form 10-K are forward-looking. We use words such as anticipates, believes, expects, future, intends, and similar expressions to identify forward-looking statements. Forward-looking statements reflect management's current expectations and are inherently uncertain. Actual results and outcomes could differ materially for a variety of reasons, including, among others, fluctuations in foreign exchange rates and energy prices, changes in global economic conditions, tariff and trade policies, resource and supply volatility, including for memory chips, and customer demand and spending, inflation, interest rates, regional labor market constraints, world events, the rate of growth of the internet, online commerce, cloud services, and new and emerging technologies, the amount that Amazon.com invests in new business opportunities and the timing of those investments, the mix of products and services sold to customers, the mix of net sales derived from products as compared with services, the extent to which we owe income or other taxes, competition, management of growth, potential fluctuations in operating results, international growth and expansion, the outcomes of claims, litigation, government investigations, and other proceedings, fulfillment, sortation, delivery, and data center optimization, risks of inventory management, variability in demand, the degree to which we enter into, maintain, and develop commercial agreements, proposed and completed acquisitions and strategic transactions, payments risks, and risks of fulfillment throughput and productivity. In addition, global economic and geopolitical conditions and additional or unforeseen circumstances, developments, or events may give rise to or amplify many of these risks. These risks and uncertainties, as well as other risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results or outcomes to differ significantly from management's expectations, are described in greater detail in Item 1A of Part I, "Risk Factors."

Our primary source of revenue is the sale of a wide range of products and services to customers. The products offered through our stores include merchandise and content we have purchased for resale and products offered by third-party sellers, and we also manufacture and sell electronic devices and produce media content. Generally, we recognize gross revenue from items we sell from our inventory as product sales and recognize our net share of revenue of items sold by third-party sellers as service sales. We seek to increase unit sales across our stores, through increased product selection, across numerous product categories. We also offer other services such as compute, storage, and database offerings, fulfillment, advertising, publishing, and digital content subscriptions.

Our financial focus is on long-term, sustainable growth in free cash flow. Free cash flow is driven primarily by increasing operating income and efficiently managing accounts receivable, inventory, accounts payable, and cash capital expenditures, including our decision to purchase or lease property and equipment. Increases in operating income primarily result from increases in sales of products and services and efficiently managing our operating costs, partially offset by investments we make in longer-term strategic initiatives, including capital expenditures focused on improving the customer experience. To increase sales of products and services, we focus on improving all aspects of the customer experience, including lowering prices, improving availability, offering faster delivery and performance times, increasing selection, producing original content, increasing product categories and service offerings, expanding product information, improving ease of use, improving reliability, and earning customer trust. See "Results of Operations — Non-GAAP Financial Measures" below for additional information on our non-GAAP free cash flow measure.

We seek to reduce our variable costs per unit and work to leverage our fixed costs. Our variable costs include product and content costs, payment processing and related transaction costs, picking, packaging, and preparing orders for shipment, transportation, customer service support, costs necessary to run AWS, and a portion of our marketing costs. Our fixed costs include the costs necessary to build and run our technology infrastructure; to build, enhance, and add features to our online stores, web services, electronic devices, and digital offerings; and to build and optimize our fulfillment network. Variable costs generally change directly with sales volume, while fixed costs generally are dependent on the timing of capacity needs, geographic expansion, category expansion, and other factors. To decrease our variable costs on a per unit basis and enable us to lower prices for customers, we seek to increase our direct sourcing, increase discounts from suppliers, and reduce defects in our processes. To minimize unnecessary growth in fixed costs, we seek to improve process efficiencies and maintain a lean culture.

We seek to turn inventory quickly and collect from consumers before our payments to vendors and sellers become due. Because consumers primarily use credit cards in our stores, our receivables from consumers settle quickly. We expect variability in inventory turnover over time since it is affected by numerous factors, including our product mix, the mix of sales by us and by third-party sellers, our continuing focus on in-stock inventory availability and selection of product offerings, supply chain disruptions and resulting vendor lead times, our investment in new geographies and product lines, and the extent to which we choose to utilize third-party fulfillment providers. We also expect some variability in accounts payable days over

time since they are affected by several factors, including the mix of product sales, the mix of sales by third-party sellers, the mix of suppliers, seasonality, and changes in payment and other terms over time, including the effect of balancing pricing and timing of payment terms with suppliers.

We expect spending in technology and infrastructure will increase over time, which can negatively impact short-term free cash flow, as we add infrastructure and employees, including to support our artificial intelligence and machine learning initiatives, to support long-term growth. Our technology and infrastructure investment and capital spending projects often support a variety of product and service offerings due to geographic expansion and the cross-functionality of our systems and operations. We seek to invest efficiently in several areas of technology and infrastructure, including AWS, and expansion of new and existing product categories and service offerings, as well as in infrastructure to enhance the customer experience and improve our process efficiencies. We believe that advances in technology, specifically the speed and reduced cost of processing power, data storage and analytics, improved wireless connectivity, and the practical applications of artificial intelligence and machine learning, will continue to improve users' experience on the internet and increase its ubiquity in people's lives. To best take advantage of these continued advances in technology, we are investing in AWS, which offers a broad set of on-demand technology services, including compute, storage, database, analytics, and machine learning, and other services to developers and enterprises of all sizes. We are also investing in initiatives to build and deploy innovative and efficient software and electronic devices as well as other initiatives including the development of a satellite network for global broadband service and autonomous vehicles for ride-hailing services.

We seek to efficiently manage shareholder dilution while maintaining the flexibility to issue shares for strategic purposes, such as financings, acquisitions, and aligning employee compensation with shareholders' interests. We utilize restricted stock units as our primary vehicle for equity compensation because we believe this compensation model aligns the long-term interests of our shareholders and employees. In measuring shareholder dilution, we include all vested and unvested stock awards outstanding, without regard to estimated forfeitures. Total shares outstanding plus outstanding stock awards were 10.9 billion and 11.0 billion as of December 31, 2024 and 2025.

Our financial reporting currency is the U.S. Dollar and changes in foreign exchange rates significantly affect our reported results and consolidated trends. For example, if the U.S. Dollar weakens year-over-year relative to currencies in our international locations, our consolidated net sales and operating expenses will be higher than if currencies had remained constant. Likewise, if the U.S. Dollar strengthens year-over-year relative to currencies in our international locations, our consolidated net sales and operating expenses will be lower than if currencies had remained constant. We believe that our increasing diversification beyond the U.S. economy through our growing international businesses benefits our shareholders over the long-term. We also believe it is useful to evaluate our operating results and growth rates before and after the effect of currency changes.

In addition, the remeasurement of our intercompany balances can result in significant gains and losses associated with the effect of movements in foreign exchange rates. Currency volatilities may continue, which may significantly impact (either positively or negatively) our reported results and consolidated trends and comparisons.

Our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 includes a discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations for the year ended December 31, 2023 in Item 7 of Part II, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations."

The preparation of financial statements in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles of the United States ("GAAP") requires estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, revenues and expenses, and related disclosures of contingent liabilities in the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes. Critical accounting estimates are those estimates made in accordance with GAAP that involve a significant level of estimation uncertainty and have had or are reasonably likely to have a material impact on the financial condition or results of operations of the Company. Based on this definition, we have identified the critical accounting estimates addressed below. We also have other key accounting policies, which involve the use of estimates, judgments, and assumptions that are significant to understanding our results. For additional information, see Item 8 of Part II, "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data — Note 1 — Description of Business, Accounting Policies, and Supplemental Disclosures." Although we believe that our estimates, assumptions, and judgments are reasonable, they are based upon information presently available. Actual results may differ significantly from these estimates under different assumptions, judgments, or conditions.

Inventories, consisting of products available for sale, are primarily accounted for using the first-in first-out method, and are valued at the lower of cost and net realizable value. This valuation requires us to make judgments, based on currently available information, about the likely method of disposition, such as through sales to individual customers, returns to product vendors, or liquidations, and expected recoverable values of each disposition category. These assumptions about future disposition of inventory are inherently uncertain and changes in our estimates and assumptions may cause us to realize material write-downs in the future. As a measure of sensitivity, for every 1% of additional inventory valuation allowance as of December 31, 2025, we would have recorded an additional cost of sales of approximately $405 million.

paragraphs: 本年度報告書及本報告書中引用的其他文件包含基於本報告書日期的預測、估計和預測的前瞻式陳述。實際結果和結果可能與前瞻式陳述中表達的內容有重大差異。請見第一部分第一項「風險因素」。本報告書中，「Amazon.com」、「我們」、「我們的」及其他類似詞包括Amazon.com, Inc.及其子公司，除非上下文另有說明。
我們力求成為地球最以客戶為中心的公司。我們遵循四個原則：以客戶為中心而非競爭對手為中心、對發明的熱愛、對運營 excellence 的承諾、以及遠見卓識。在每個分部中，我們服務我們的主要客戶羣體，包括消費者、賣家、開發者、企業、內容創作者、廣告商和員工。
我們將運作組織化為三個分部：北美、國際和Amazon Web Services（「AWS」）。這些分部反映了公司評估業務表現和管理運作的方式。有關我們淨銷售額的資訊包含於第二部分第八項，「財務報表及附註 — 論述 10 — 分部資訊」。

我們通過線上和實體商店服務消費者，專注於選項、價格和便利性。我們設計商店以使我們和第三方能夠在 dozens 個產品類別中銷售數十億個獨特產品。客戶通過我們的網站、移動應用程式、Alexa、設備、串流和親自訪問我們的商店來訪問我們的產品。我們還製造和銷售電子設備，包括Kindle、Fire平板電腦、Fire電視、Echo、Ring、Blink和eero，並開發和生産媒體內容。我們力求為客戶提供低價格、快速且免費的配送、易於使用的功能和及時的客戶服務。此外，我們還提供訂閱服務，如Amazon Prime，這是一個包括數十萬項商品免費配送、獲獎電影和節目、實時運動和其他福利的會員計劃。
我們通過多種方式履行客戶訂單，包括：我們運作的北美和國際履行網路；某些國家的協作和委外安排；數位交付；以及通過我們的實體商店。我們在全球運作客戶服務中心，這些中心通過協作安排進行補充。請見第一部分第二項，「財產」。
我們提供計劃，使賣家能夠成長其業務、在我們商店銷售產品並使用我們的服務履行訂單。在這些交易中，我們不是賣家的記錄持有人。我們因賣家計劃而獲得固定費用、銷售百分比、每單位活動費用、利息或上述各項的組合。
我們通過AWS服務開發者和企業，包括創業公司、政府機構和學術機構，提供一系列即時技術服務，包括計算、存儲、數據庫、分析、人工智能和機器學習及其他服務。
我們提供計劃，使作者、獨立出版商、音樂家、電影製作人、Twitch串流者、技能和應用開發者及其他人士能夠發佈和銷售內容。
我們為賣家、零售商、發行商、作者及其他人士提供廣告服務，透過如贊助廣告、展示廣告及影片廣告等計劃。

我們的業務涵蓋多種產品類型、服務項目及配送渠道。我們在全球市場中競爭激烈，市場環境正在迅速變化，我們面臨來自世界各地不同行業的廣泛競爭對手。我們的當前及潛在競爭對手包括：(1) 物理零售商、電商零售商、全渠道零售商、發行商、零售商、製造商及生產商；(2) 物理、數位及互動媒體的發行商、製造商及零售商；(3) 網路搜尋引擎、比價購物網站、社羣網路、網際網路門戶、虛擬助理及其他線上及應用程式基於的發現、使用或獲取貨品及服務的方式，包括直接或與其他零售商合作，包括透過人工智慧；(4) 提供電商服務的公司，包括網站開發及託管、全渠道銷售、存貨及供應鏈管理、廣告、履行、客戶服務及支付處理；(5) 提供履行及物流服務的公司，無論線上或線下；(6) 提供資訊科技服務或產品的公司，包括現場或雲端基礎設施、人工智慧相關工具及服務及其他服務；(7) 設計、製造、行銷或銷售消費電子、通訊及其他電子設備及服務的公司；(8) 在線上及實體商店銷售食品產品的公司；(9) 提供廣告服務的公司，無論在數位或其他格式；(10) 提供虛擬或實體醫療服務的公司。我們認為，我們零售業務的主要競爭因素包括選項、價格及便利性，包括快速及可靠的履行。我們賣家及企業服務的其他競爭因素包括我們服務及工具的品質、速度及可靠性，以及客戶改變業務實踐的能力及意願。我們當前及潛在競爭對手中，有些具有更大的資源、更悠久的歷史、更多的客戶、更高的品牌認知度及對我們各個業務關鍵輸入的更大控制。他們可能從供應商那裡獲得更佳的條款，採用更具攻擊性的價格，追求限制我們對供應的限制性分銷協議，將消費者導向自己的產品而非我們的產品，通過限制性條款鎖定潛在客戶，並在技術、基礎設施、履行及市場推廣方面投入更多資源。互聯網及其他技術包括人工智慧促進競爭進入及比價購物，這增強了新、小或較不知名的企業對我們的競爭能力。我們的每個業務也受到快速變化及新商業模式的發展和新資金充足的競爭對手進入的影響。其他公司也可能進入業務合併或聯盟，以強化其競爭地位。
我們認為我們的商標、服務標誌、著作權、專利、網域名稱、商標樣式、商業祕密、專有技術及其他類似智慧財產權對我們成功至關重要，我們依靠商標法、著作權法、專利法、商業祕密保護、保密及/或授權協議來保護我們的專有權。我們已註冊或申請註冊多個美國及國際網域名稱、商標、服務標誌及著作權。此外，我們已提交了多個美國及國際專利申請，覆蓋我們的部分專有技術。
我們的業務受到季節性影響，歷史性地在第四季度，即每年12月31日結束的季度，銷售量會更高。
我們的員工對我們成為地球最以客戶為中心的公司至關重要。截至2025年12月31日，我們約僱用了1,576,000名全職和兼職員工。此外，我們使用獨立承包商和臨時人員來補充我們的人力資源。具備資質的人才競爭激烈，特別是軟體工程師、計算機科學家及其他技術人員（包括人工智慧和機器學習技術），受制於勞動市場的緊張也增加了我們業務其他部分的人才競爭。

我們 strive to be Earth's best employer. We rely on numerous and evolving initiatives to implement this objective and invent mechanisms for talent development, including competitive pay and benefits, flexible work arrangements, and skills training and educational programs such as Amazon Career Choice (education funding for eligible employees). Over 300,000 Amazon employees around the world have participated in Career Choice. We also continue to inspect and refine the mechanisms we use to hire, develop, evaluate, and retain our employees. In addition, safety is integral to everything we do at Amazon and we continue to invest in safety improvements such as capital improvements, new safety technology, vehicle safety controls, and engineering ergonomic solutions. Our safety team is dedicated to using the science of safety to solve complex problems and establish new industry best practices. We also provide mentorship and support resources to our employees, and have deployed numerous programs that advance employee engagement, communication, and feedback.

paragraphs: 本年度報告書（Form 10-K）包含根據1995年私人證券訴訟改革法（Private Securities Litigation Reform Act）的含意而作出的前瞻性陳述。本報告書中除歷史事實陳述之外的所有陳述，包括關於指導意見、行業前景或未來營運或財務狀況結果的陳述，均屬前瞻性陳述。我們使用如預期、認為、預期、未來、意圖及類似表達的詞彙來識別前瞻性陳述。前瞻性陳述反映管理層當前的預期，並固有地具有不確定性。實際結果和結果可能會因多種原因而與管理層的預期大不相同，包括但不限於外匯匯率和能源價格的波動、全球經濟條件的變化、關稅和貿易政策的變化、資源和供應波動，包括記憶體晶片，以及客戶需求和支出的變化、通脹、利率、區域勞動市場制約、世界事件、互聯網增長率、線上商販、雲服務和新興技術的增長，Amazon.com在新業務機會上的投資額及其投資時間，銷售給客戶的產品和服務的組合，產品銷售與服務銷售的收入組合，我們欠付的利息或其他稅款的 extent，競爭、管理增長、營運結果的潛在波動、國際增長和擴張、訴訟、政府調查及其他程序的結果、履行、分揀、遞送和資料中心優化、存貨管理風險、需求變動的變異性、我們進入、維持和開發商業協議的程度、擬議和完成的收購和戰略交易、付款風險以及履行通過量和生產力的風險。此外，全球經濟和地緣政治條件以及其他或未預見的情況、發展或事件可能會導致這些風險的產生或放大。這些風險和不確定性，以及可能導致我們實際結果或結果與管理層預期有顯著差異的其他風險和不確定性，詳述於本報告書第一部分第1A項「風險因素」中。

我們的主要收入來源是向客戶銷售各種產品和服務。通過我們的商店銷售的產品包括我們購買以供銷售的貨品和內容，以及由第三方賣家銷售的產品，我們還製造和銷售電子設備並生産媒體內容。一般而言，我們在銷售我們存貨中的項目時確認銷售收入，並將第三方賣家銷售的項目確認為服務收入。我們通過增加產品選擇、跨多個產品類別來增加商店的單位銷售。我們還提供其他服務，如計算、存儲和數據庫服務、履行、廣告、出版和數位內容訂閱。

我們的財務重點是長期、可持續的自由現金流增長。自由現金流主要由增加營運收入和有效地管理應收帳款、存貨、應付帳款和現金資本支出驅動，包括我們購買或租賃財產和設備的決定。營運收入的增加主要來自產品和服務銷售的增加以及有效地管理我們的營運成本，部分抵消了我們在長期戰略項目上的投資，包括專注於改善客戶體驗的資本支出。為了增加產品和服務的銷售，我們專注於改善所有方面的客戶體驗，包括降低價格、提高可獲取性、提供更快的遞送和性能時間、增加選擇、生産原創內容、增加產品類別和服務供應、擴大產品信息、改善易用性、改善可靠性以及獲得客戶信任。請見「營運結果—非GAAP財務指標」部分，以獲取我們非GAAP自由現金流指標的更多資訊。

我們力求減少每單位的變動成本並努力利用固定成本。我們的變動成本包括產品和內容成本、支付處理及相關交易成本、揀選、包裝和準備訂單供運送、運輸、客戶服務支持、運行AWS的必要成本以及我們市場費用的一部分。我們的固定成本包括建設和運行我們的技術基礎設施的成本；建設、升級和添加功能到我們的線上商店、網上服務、電子設備和數位供應；以及建設和優化我們的履行網路的成本。變動成本一般會隨著銷售量的變化而變化，而固定成本一般取決於容量需求的時間、地理擴張、類別擴張及其他因素。為了減少每單位的變動成本並使我們能夠降低客戶的價格，我們力求增加直接採購、從供應商獲得折扣以及減少我們流程中的缺陷。為了最小化不必要的固定成本增長，我們力求提高流程效率並維持精益文化。

我們力求迅速轉換存貨並在付款給供應商和賣家之前從消費者那裡收錢。由於消費者主要在我們商店使用信用卡，我們從消費者那裡的應收帳款結算迅速。我們預期存貨週轉率會隨著時間而變動，因為它受到多種因素的影響，包括我們的產品組合、我們和第三方賣家的銷售組合、我們繼續關注在庫存貨的可獲得性和產品選擇、供應鏈中斷和由此導致的供應商交貨時間、我們在新地理區域和產品線上的投資，以及我們選擇利用第三方履行服務提供商的程度。我們也預期隨著時間的推移，應付帳款天數會有些變動，因為它受到多種因素的影響，包括產品銷售的組合、第三方賣家的銷售組合、供應商的組合、季節性以及隨著時間推移而發生的付款和其他條款的變化，包括與供應商平衡價格和付款條款的影響。

本公司的技術和基礎設施支出預計將隨著時間增加，這可能會對短期自由現金流產生負面影響，因為我們將投資於基礎設施和員工，包括支持我們的人工智慧和機器學習計劃，以支持長期增長。本公司在技術和基礎設施方面的投資和資本支出項目通常支持多種產品和服務的提供，這得益於地理擴張和我們系統和運作的跨功能性。我們希望在幾個技術和基礎設施領域高效地投資，包括AWS，以及新舊產品類別和服務的擴展，以及投資於基礎設施以增強客戶體驗和提高我們的流程效率。我們認為，技術的進步，特別是處理能力、數據存儲和分析的加速以及數據存儲和分析的成本降低、改善無線連接以及人工智慧和機器學習的實用應用，將繼續改善用戶在互聯網上的體驗並增加其在人們生活中的普及率。為了充分利用這些技術的繼續進步，我們正在投資於AWS，這提供了一個廣泛的即時技術服務套件，包括計算、存儲、數據庫、分析和機器學習，以及其他開發者和企業的服務。我們還正在投資於建設和部署創新和高效的軟體和電子設備以及其他計劃，包括開發全球寬帶服務的衛星網路和出車服務的自主車輛。

我們希望在保持發行股權的靈活性以進行戰略性目的（如融資、收購和將員工薪酬與股東利益對齊）的同時，有效地管理股權稀釋。我們使用受限制的股票單位作為我們主要的股權補償工具，因為我們認為這種補償模式與股東和員工的長期利益對齊。在衡量股權稀釋時，我們包括所有已授予和未授予的股權獎勵，不考慮預計的回贖。截至2024年12月31日和2025年12月31日，流通股數和未授予的股權獎勵總數分別為10.9億股和11.0億股。

本公司財務報告幣種為美金，外幣匯率的變動顯著影響本公司報告結果及合併趨勢。例如，若本年度美元相對於本公司國際據點的貨幣相對變弱，本公司合併淨銷售額及營業費用將會比貨幣保持不變的情況下更高。反之，若本年度美元相對於本公司國際據點的貨幣相對變強，本公司合併淨銷售額及營業費用將會比貨幣保持不變的情況下更低。本公司認為，通過我們成長中的國際業務，我們在美國經濟之外的多元化增加，長期而言對股東有利。我們也認為，在評估我們的營運結果和增長率之前和之後考慮貨幣變動的影響是有用的。
此外，本公司對內部帳戶餘額的重新衡量可能會導致與外幣匯率變動影響相關的顯著利得和損失。匯率波動可能會繼續，這可能會顯著影響（either positively or negatively）本公司報告結果及合併趨勢和比較。
有關上述每個項目更多詳細資訊，請參閱第二部分第8項，"財務報告及附註 — 請求1 — 本公司業務描述、會計原則及補充披露"
本公司於2024年12月31日結束年度的10-K年度報告包括第二部分第7項，"經理人對財務狀況及營運結果的討論及分析"中，本公司財務狀況及2023年度營運結果的討論及分析。

按照美國通用會計原則（"GAAP"）準備財務報告需要進行估計和假設，這些估計和假設影響合併財務報表及附註中資產、負債、收入、費用及相關披露的報告數額。關鍵會計估計是指按照GAAP進行的估計，涉及重大估計不確定性，且對本公司財務狀況或營運結果有重大影響的估計。根據此定義，我們已識別出以下關鍵會計估計。我們還有其他關鍵會計原則，這些原則涉及使用估計、判斷和假設，這些假設對理解我們的結果很重要。有關詳情，請參閱第二部分第8項，"財務報告及附註 — 請求1 — 本公司業務描述、會計原則及補充披露"。儘管我們認為我們的估計、假設和判斷是合理的，但這些估計、假設和判斷是基於目前可獲取的資訊。實際結果可能在不同的假設、判斷或條件下與這些估計有顯著差異。

存貨，包括可供銷售的產品，主要按照先進先出法進行會計處理，並以成本和可實現淨值中較低者計價。此計價需要我們基於目前可獲取的資訊，對存貨的處置方法進行判斷，例如通過個人客戶銷售、返還給產品供應商或清算，以及每個處置類別的預期可回收價值。關於未來存貨處置的這些假設具有固有的不確定性，我們的估計和假設的變化可能會導致我們在未來實現重大減損。作為敏感性測試，對於2025年12月31日存貨增值準備額增加1%，我們將會記錄約4.05億美元的銷售費用。

paragraphs: 請謹慎考慮下列關於重大因素、事件和不確定性之討論，這些因素、事件和不確定性可能會使投資於我們的證券風險增加。本文件中所討論的這些風險因素可能會在本公司可能或可能無法準確預測、辨識或控制的情況下，對本公司之業務、成長、聲譽、前景、財務狀況、營運結果（包括財務結果之各項組成部分）、現金流量、流動性及股票價格產生重大不利影響。這些風險因素並未列舉本公司所面臨之所有風險；本公司之業務也可能受到現行未知或本公司目前未認為對本公司業務構成重大風險之因素、事件或不確定性之影響。除本文件第二部分第7項「管理層對財務狀況及營運結果之討論與分析」中所討論之因素外，全球經濟及地緣政治環境及其他或未預見之情況、發展或事件可能會導致或放大本文件中所討論之許多風險。本文件中所列之許多風險也可能影響本公司之客戶，包括第三方賣家，這可能會間接對本公司產生重大不利影響。本節之披露反映本公司對未來可能對本公司產生重大不利影響之因素之信念和意見。過去事件之提及僅供示範之用，並非意圖列舉完整之清單或表示該因素過去是否發生。

本公司之業務正在迅速發展且競爭激烈，我們在全球各地都有競爭對手，包括跨境競爭，以及在物理零售、電商、全渠道零售、電商服務、網際網路及基礎設施計算服務、電子設備、數位內容、廣告、超市、醫療保健、通訊及運輸和物流服務等不同行業中。我們的一些現有及潛在競爭對手在資源、歷史、客戶數量或品牌認知度方面可能更具優勢，特別是對於我們的新產品和服務以及在新地理區域。他們可能從供應商那裡獲得更好的條款，採用更具攻擊性的價格策略，並在技術、基礎設施、履行和市場推廣方面投入更多資源。

競爭繼續加劇，包括新商業模式的發展和新資金充裕的競爭對手的進入，以及我們的競爭對手進入業務合併或聯盟，以及其他市場段落的established公司擴大業務以與本公司競爭。此外，包括搜尋、網際網路及基礎設施計算服務、人工智慧和機器學習的實際應用、數位內容、衛星和電子設備等新和升級技術繼續增加我們的競爭。互聯網及其他技術，包括人工智慧，促進競爭進入和比價購物，這增強了新、小或較不知名企業對我們的競爭能力。由於競爭，我們的產品和服務可能不成功，我們可能會失敗於獲取或失去業務，我們可能會被要求增加支出或降低價格，這可能會對我們的銷售和利潤產生重大影響。
我們可能在較新的市場段落中缺乏經驗，而我們的客戶可能不會採用我們的產品或服務。這些產品或服務可能會提出新的和困難的技術挑戰，如果這些產品或服務的客戶經歷服務中斷、延遲、挫敗或失敗或

品質問題，我們可能會受到主張。此外，如果有的話，我們在較新活動中的盈利或其他預期利益可能未能達到我們的預期，我們可能不足以在這些較新活動中取得足夠的成功以回報我們在這些活動中的投資，這些投資通常很大。未能實現我們在新技術、產品或服務上投資的效益可能會導致這些投資的價值被寫下或寫掉。此外，我們的永續發展計劃可能因多種原因而失敗，包括我們無法實現新技術的預期效益或我們未能成功規劃或執行新策略，這可能會損害我們的業務或損害我們的聲譽。
本公司之國際活動對我們的收入和利潤至關重要，我們計劃進一步擴大國際業務。在某些國際市場段落中，我們的運營經驗相對有限，可能無法從首個進入市場的優勢中獲益或否則會失敗。建立、發展和維護國際業務和商店以及在國際上推廣本公司品牌是昂貴的。本公司之國際業務可能無法在長期內實現盈利。
